title: Internet Infrastructure: Georgia and Israel deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Two different countries, two sets of rules. Pick the country first, then use that country’s list in every module. Check with a local expert.
Written terms and signed copies for every helper, even part-time.
Compare three models: build and own, lease from a carrier, or share with a partner. Judge each by cost per connected site.
Plan the people and partners: a licensed installer, a power supplier, a site owner, and a support person.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep a risk list with a response for each; include a rules change. Check with a local expert.
Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit; many founders need flexible support in more than one language.
Add tax and duty explicitly; never bury them in a price. Check with a local expert.
Check the spectrum, cable-route, tower and telecom licence rules with the regulator before any build. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Register and license Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep a local address and a named contact in the country where you trade.
Trust: registration number, address, delivery days and a refund note on every page. Check with a local expert.
Launch with a go or no-go rule: 40 paying sites in 3 months and uptime above 98%. Check with a local expert.
Price per site: build cost spread over years, plus running cost, plus margin. Calculate the payback.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Say in plain words what you collect and why; give a way to see and correct it.
Partner with a local college, chamber or training body to find helpers and to practise.
Freelancers are common: write scope, price, language and date in one page.
Public holidays and the working week differ; put the working days on every delivery promise.

Languages differ by customer: write the page in the local language plus English.
